output.summary: Approve dual-layer Implementation review: language-agnostic and language-specific quality nodes and fast checks.

approvedRows.question: Should CodeWiki implement both language-agnostic and language-specific quality nodes and fast checks?
approvedRows.currentState: The sprint already approves a language-agnostic evidence protocol and a fast-check versus exit-node split, but it does not explicitly require both language-neutral and language-specific review layers in both phases.
approvedRows.desiredState: Implementation review has dual layers: language-agnostic quality nodes and fast checks for universal evidence contracts, plus language-specific quality nodes and fast checks for ecosystem semantics.
approvedRows.rationale: The language-agnostic layer protects portability and common false-pass risks; language-specific layers provide deeper semantic evidence that generic diagnostics cannot capture.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users in every language get baseline review, while supported languages get sharper feedback and fewer false passes.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers must keep the common layer stable and add language-specific packs incrementally with tests and bounded budgets.
approvedRows.routeRationale: This expands planning scope and must become explicit work units before implementation.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: Both layers are necessary: generic checks alone miss language semantics, while language-specific checks alone break portability.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: User explicitly states both language-agnostic and language-specific nodes and fast checks must be implemented.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Dual-layer review fits the quality-network model and preserves language neutrality without sacrificing precision.
agentAssessment.rationale: The architecture cleanly maps to shared evidence plus adapter-specific runners.
concerns: Plan must avoid implementing every language at once; begin with generic layer and one thin language pack.

approvedRows.currentPain: A single generic review layer would miss language semantics; a single language-specific layer would violate CodeWiki portability.
approvedRows.desiredOutcome: Review standards and fast checks are split into common and language-specific layers with shared normalized evidence.
approvedRows.successSignal: Planning includes work units for common evidence/check nodes and separate language-specific pack scaffolding, with tests proving both can run together.
nonGoals: Do not implement every language adapter in the first sprint.
Do not make language-specific packs required for baseline CodeWiki review.
Do not let language-specific tools override CodeWiki semantic authority.

qualityStandards.description: Every planned work ref is covered by implementation evidence and no unknown planning refs are introduced.
Implementation changes stay inside planned component/path scope and existing repo paths.
Every planned acceptance criterion is covered by structured evidence refs.
Required implementation checks are structured, present, passing, cover planned verification, and package changes include pack verification.
Required red/green TDD evidence is mapped to planned acceptance criteria.
Implementation output has change-level and aggregate content proof when required.
Worker-produced evidence is tied to active runtime claims and completed worker results.
Changed source/test paths align with source-map component ownership and test coverage.
Agent assessment records maintainability, simplicity, project style, and error-handling readiness.
Independent judge verifies implementation evidence actually supports the claimed changes and acceptance criteria.
Independent judge verifies passing checks are relevant to changed behavior rather than generic or unrelated proof.
Independent judge verifies the production-readiness assessment is specific and not hand-wavy.
No unresolved implementation uncertainty remains; planning, decision, or user authority is routed instead of drifting.
Security/privacy-sensitive changes include explicit review evidence.
UI/page changes include accessibility review evidence.
Dependency-surface changes include risk review evidence.
Release, publication, destructive, or externally visible implementation refs require explicit user approval.
Implementation refs are canonical trace, KB, Git, digest, source, or test refs.
